source_documents.title: A Computational Protocol to Predict Anti-Kasha Emissions: The Case of Azulene Derivatives
Excited state dynamics of azulene and its derivatives: The impact of energy gap and vibronic coupling on anti-Kasha emission in solution

reference_evidence_units.quote: transition emission has been recorded on excitation at 220, 237, 269, 296 and 315 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: azulene
reference_evidence_units.statement: Only S2 emission; no S1 emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Azulene photophysics is a true exception to Kasha’s rule as has been reported.
reference_evidence_units.subject: azulene
reference_evidence_units.statement: Azulene is a true anti-Kasha emitter (S2-S1 gap 14000 cm-1).

reference_evidence_units.quote: by 20 ps 90.5 % of the excited molecules occupy the S2 state, whereas 9.5 % occupy the S1 state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: azulene
reference_evidence_units.statement: Slow S2→S1 conversion across the large gap.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the fluorescence yield from S2 is at least 1500 times larger than the yield from S1.
reference_evidence_units.subject: azulenes 1a-e

reference_evidence_units.quote: for azulene derivatives, intersystem crossing processes among other possible non-radiative decay pathways are not relevant.
reference_evidence_units.subject: azulenes 1a-e
reference_evidence_units.statement: ISC excluded from the decay model.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The rate of the non-radiative decay of the S2 state for all compounds correlates well with the decrease of their anti-Kasha photoluminescence quantum yield
reference_evidence_units.subject: azulene and 2-substituted derivatives
reference_evidence_units.statement: S2 nonradiative loss tracks the PLQY order.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The large S2-S1 gap slows S2→S1 internal conversion so that S2 radiation competes; S1 decays nonradiatively.
